look.plainEnglish: A look is a question you ask on purpose. A rifle asks when you fire or aim. Third-person use asks from the interact button. A hunter asks on a short timer, and a loud sound calls that same look. A strategy team asks a few times a second. None of those ask from the frame loop.
look.whyGame: A query every frame, for every pawn, is how a listen server falls over, and it keeps asking through a pause.

expansions.title: A rifle
expansions.detail: The shot or the aim starts the trace at the camera.

expansions.title: A hunter
expansions.detail: The timer is the glimpse. A bottle calls the same event.

expansions.title: A team
expansions.detail: Reveal writes what the team can see. A walking camp does not.

quiz.prompt: A first-person rifle needs to know what is under the crosshair. When does it trace?
choices: When the player fires or aims
On every drawn frame, even while idle
When the animation blueprint wants a gait
When a widget paints the crosshair
quiz.why: The shot and the aim are the questions.

quiz.prompt: The line that starts a rifle trace uses the camera location. What does that origin match?
quiz.why: The player aims with the camera.

quiz.prompt: Third-person use is about to trace. Where should it start?
choices: At the camera, along the crosshair
At the chest, which hits cover the camera can see past
At the ally walking beside you
quiz.why: A chest trace lights the wrong actor.

quiz.prompt: You move every look onto the frame loop so nothing feels late. What keeps running during a pause?
choices: The queries, for pawns that are standing still
No query at all, if a frame loop always paused
quiz.why: An event can stop. A raw frame query is easy to leave on.

quiz.prompt: A bottle hits the floor near a hunter. What should the bottle call?
choices: The same Sense the glimpse timer uses
The strategy reveal for a different team
quiz.why: One look, so the stalk reads one flag.

quiz.prompt: A strategy camp stays unseen until the vision pass marks that cell.
quiz.why: Reveal writes vision. Walking does not.

quiz.prompt: Which interval matches a strategy team's glimpse?
The animation blueprint traces to rediscover a gait the movement graph already wrote. What do you delete?
quiz.why: Read the value. Do not ask again.

quiz.prompt: A horror hunter and a strategy team both 'look'. What is different?
choices: The hunter writes an alert flag
No difference, if both wrote the same float
The team looks from the player's fire button
The hunter looks only when the player presses use

quiz.prompt: Which line is a look that waits for the player, not a timer?
choices: The interact trace that runs when the use action fires
quiz.why: Use is a press. The other two are timers.

interface.plainEnglish: One function name beats a cast list. Doors and switches answer Interact. A tank and a squad answer ReceiveOrder. A key and a fuel can answer AddToSlot. The graph looks the function up once.
interface.whyGame: A new prop from art does nothing until someone edits the cast list, which is how content waits on a programmer.

expansions.title: A door
expansions.detail: It implements Interact. The trace does not name the door class.

expansions.title: A squad
expansions.detail: It implements ReceiveOrder. The click does not name the squad class.

expansions.title: A key
expansions.detail: It implements the slot add. The overlap does not cast to the key.

quiz.prompt: A door, a rifle on the ground, and a switch all need use. What do they implement?
choices: A cast chain, one class each
The order function a squad uses

quiz.prompt: ProcessEvent on Interact runs after a hit. What does the call accomplish?
choices: It calls the hit actor's own use function
It casts to every prop class until one works

quiz.prompt: Art adds a new wall switch. What does the existing use graph change?
choices: Nothing, if the switch implements Interact
A new cast to the switch class

quiz.prompt: The use graph casts to each prop class. What fails when the tenth prop arrives?
choices: That prop never responds, until a programmer adds another cast

quiz.prompt: A tank and a rifle squad both receive a right-click. Which function do both implement?
choices: The use function a door implements
quiz.why: An order is not a use.

quiz.prompt: A key and a fuel can can enter inventory through the same slot call.
Which call belongs to a pickup rather than a door?
quiz.why: The overlap adds. The door answers use.

quiz.prompt: A horror fuse and a strategy tank both get clicked. Why are their functions different?
choices: A fuse is used, and a tank is ordered
They must share one function name
Both should cast from the same graph
The tank should answer Interact and ignore selection
quiz.why: Use and order are different questions.

quiz.prompt: The graph looks the function up once. What does a beginner often write instead?
choices: A data row for a cost

quiz.prompt: Which line is the shared use, not a cast?
choices: A cast to the door class, then a custom pin
A cast to the switch class
A cast to the rifle class

authority.plainEnglish: A shared number has one writer. Health, a limb, supplies, score, shells, the equipped id, and relevance are all that kind of number. The write sits inside the authority check. A client that writes early will snap when the server answers.
authority.whyGame: Two writers make two machines disagree about a body, a stock, or which weapon is in the hands.

expansions.title: Health
expansions.detail: The sample 90 is a stand-in inside the check, not a client write.

expansions.title: The equipped id
expansions.detail: Proxies build the mesh from the server id.

expansions.title: A limb
expansions.detail: A bruise stops at 10 percent. The server applies it.

quiz.prompt: Which numbers need a single writer?
choices: Health, supplies, score, shells, the equipped id, and relevance
The spring-arm mesh and the mapping context
The camera boom length on one machine

quiz.prompt: The sample assigns Health = 90.f inside HasAuthority. Where must that assignment sit?
choices: Inside the check, not on the line after an empty one
On every client, so the flash is early
quiz.why: An empty check does not wrap the write.

quiz.prompt: The server writes health. What should other machines do when the value arrives?
choices: Ignore it and keep their local number
Write it back to the server
quiz.why: The notify presents. It does not recompute.

quiz.prompt: A client spends supplies so the number drops immediately. What do the other machines still show?
choices: The old stock, until the authority write arrives
A wiped stock, as if a mismatch cleared it
quiz.why: The private spend is not the stock.

quiz.prompt: A proxy shows a rifle the server did not equip. Where was the id written?
quiz.why: The mesh follows the server id.

quiz.prompt: A client may write Relevant so its own pawn stays smooth.
A bruise on a limb of max 50 should stop where?
choices: At 5, unless the hit is a real down
Back at the maximum, if limbs could not change

quiz.prompt: Shells and supplies both decrease during a battle. Why are they still two writes?
choices: A barrage must not bankrupt the base
They are the same float under two names
Only the client may touch either

quiz.prompt: Which line is an authority write of a selection?
choices: EquippedId assigned from the equip action inside the check
A client write of the same id
quiz.why: The id is shared. The flash is not.

quiz.prompt: Score is added on the client that saw the kill. What is the board showing?
choices: A number the host never granted

data.plainEnglish: A literal in a graph is a designer number pretending to be code. A building's cost and a medal's points belong on rows. A key stacks to one and a fuel can stacks higher, and that cap lives on the item.
data.whyGame: Sharing the literal 25 makes a barracks and a turret cost the same, and sharing 10 makes every medal worth the same.

expansions.title: A barracks
expansions.detail: Its row names the cost. The spend reads the row.

expansions.title: A medal
expansions.detail: A kill and a capture do not have to be worth 10.

expansions.title: A fuel can
expansions.detail: The stack cap sits on the item, beside the name.

quiz.prompt: A barracks and a turret should not cost the same. Where do the two costs live?
choices: As one literal 25 in the spend graph
Inside the authority check as comments

quiz.prompt: The excerpt spends Supplies minus 25. What does that 25 stand for?
choices: A sample cost a row should replace
The required price of every building
How many rounds fit in the gun

quiz.prompt: A kill and a capture both award points. What should differ?
choices: No difference, if both added ten
Which client is allowed to award

quiz.prompt: You leave 10 in the award graph for every result. What becomes impossible?
choices: A capture that is worth more than a kill

quiz.prompt: A key stacks to one and a fuel can stacks higher. Where is that difference?
choices: As a magic number in the overlap
In the medal asset by accident

quiz.prompt: MagSize in the reload clamp is the same kind of mistake as a typed building cost.
quiz.why: The clamp's cap is the right shape. 25 and 10 are the literals to move.

quiz.prompt: Which number in the beginner samples should move onto a row?
choices: The magazine compared with its cap

quiz.prompt: A designer retunes a turret from 40 to 60. What should they edit?
The overlap only checks that the stack count is positive. What still belongs beside that test?
choices: A second literal for every item class

quiz.prompt: Which pair is a sample literal versus a cap that already has the right shape?
choices: The medal's 10, versus MagSize in the reload clamp
Two copies of the building cost
The stick check versus the camera origin
